fixes.explanation: That's it. Solomon, David's son and Israel's king (Proverbs 1:1), says the plans of the heart belong to man, but the reply of the tongue is from the LORD. Man brings the plan and the reply comes from the LORD. I plan a whole batch in my head, and then I open my mouth and something else entirely comes out. Humans plan, friend, and I'm the proof.

Learning on their own isn't in the verse. Solomon says everyone who is proud in heart is detestable to the LORD, and he adds, "be assured that he will not go unpunished" (Proverbs 16:5). That's the part the verse says about the proud. It's a serious one, so I'll leave it plain.

Good counsel is helpful, but this verse doesn't name the elders. Solomon says that by the fear of the LORD one turns aside from evil (Proverbs 16:6). The fear of the LORD means honoring Him so much that you steer away from what He hates. That's how a person turns aside, according to this verse.

Strength of hand isn't in this verse. Solomon says that by the fear of the LORD one turns aside from evil (Proverbs 16:6). Turning aside from evil comes by the fear of the LORD, not by muscle. My mustache does all my lifting, and even it can't turn me from evil by force.

Plenty with hard work isn't one of the options Solomon weighs. He says, "Better a little with righteousness than great gain with injustice." Notice what he puts on the scale: how a person got it, not just how much. The better one is the little with righteousness.

That's the word. A man's heart plans his course, but the LORD determines his steps (Proverbs 16:9). The heart draws the map and the LORD determines the steps. I never planned on a junk drawer, but I'd say my steps got determined, and I ended up in a bakery on a cookie planet.

Solomon says the opposite. Honest scales and balances are from the LORD, and all the weights in the bag are His concern (Proverbs 16:11). Every weight in that bag is His concern. So the statement is false.
Correct. Solomon says honest scales and balances are from the LORD, and "all the weights in the bag are His concern." Every weight in the bag is His concern. Honest weights matter to Him.

Kings do show up in this chapter, so I see why you picked the court. But Solomon says the highway of the upright leads away from evil (Proverbs 16:17). That's where it heads. The king's court isn't mentioned in this verse.

That's the word. Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall (Proverbs 16:18). Pride walks in first and a fall follows. I once strutted across my bakery like I owned the place and slid face-first into the chocolate chips.

That's the word. Understanding is a fountain of life to its possessor, but the discipline of fools is folly (Proverbs 16:22). A fountain of life on one side and folly on the other. Solomon sets the two side by side so you can see the difference.

Strength isn't what the verse gives the fool. Solomon says the discipline of fools is folly (Proverbs 16:22). He sets that against understanding, which is a fountain of life to its possessor. One side gives life and the other side is folly, and that's the contrast the blank is after.

Yes! "Pleasant words are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul and healing to the bones." Solomon says a kind word does good for the whole person, soul and bones (Proverbs 16:24). Sweet to the soul and healing to the bones is a lot for a few words to do. Pleasant words are worth handing out.

Yes. Gray hair is a crown of glory, and Solomon says it is attained along the path of righteousness (Proverbs 16:31). It's a glad line in a chapter with some heavy ones. The crown comes along that path.

That's the word. "He who is slow to anger is better than a warrior, and he who controls his temper is greater than one who captures a city." (Proverbs 16:32). Controlling your temper is called greater than capturing a city. It's harder than it sounds, especially when the oven door slams on your mustache.

A merchant isn't in this verse. Solomon says he who is slow to anger is better than a warrior, and he who controls his temper is greater than one who captures a city (Proverbs 16:32). One line names a warrior and the other names someone who captures a city. The word for the blank is warrior.

Yes. "The lot is cast into the lap, but its every decision is from the LORD." It looks like chance, but Solomon says every decision of the lot is from Him. A lot was a way of making a choice by casting it. So the answer is the LORD.
